body: ## Scope
Invoices still unpaid after their due date, once any automatic payment retries have finished. Payments that fail during a payment-processor incident are retried automatically and are not overdue; this page doesn't apply to them.
## Schedule
| Days past due | Step |
|---|---|
| 3 | Reminder email to the billing contact |
| 10 | Second reminder; account team copied |
| 21 | Final notice |
| 45 | Hosted API access suspended until paid |
## Changes from 2026
From 1 January 2027 the final notice is sent on day 21 instead of day 30.

content: ## Purpose
This page sets the 2027 monthly close for usage-based invoices: when each month's invoices are cut, which usage lands in which invoice period, and how late usage is handled. Billing Ops, Telemetry and Support use it when a customer asks what a month's invoice covers.
## Monthly close calendar
| Business day | Step | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| BD1 | Usage for the closed month is frozen in the metering warehouse | Telemetry |
| BD2 | Usage is rated against the account's price book and invoice lines are drafted | Billing Ops |
| BD3 | Variance review: lines more than 25% above the prior month are checked against usage | Billing Ops |
| BD4 | Invoices are issued and autopay is attempted on the due date shown on the invoice | Billing Ops |
| BD5 | Revenue for the month is booked and the period is closed | Accounting |"}, {"source": "sources/google_drive/shared_drives/finance/2027-close-calendar-and-invoice-periods.json", "chunk": "2/4", "kind": "Drive doc", "title": "2027 Close Calendar and Invoice Periods", "status": "final", "date": "2027-02-22", "text": "(continued) ## Monthly close calendar
Contracted accounts invoiced in arrears follow the same calendar; prepaid commitments are drawn down on BD2.
## Invoice periods and billing timezones
Until February 2027 every invoice period ran on UTC. From March 2027 usage onward, an account's invoice period runs from midnight to midnight in the account's billing timezone (`billing_timezone` on the account record; UTC unless set). A request belongs to the billing month, and to the invoice line, in which its timestamp falls in that timezone. For an account on America/Los_Angeles, a request at 03:00 UTC on 1 April 2027 is 20:00 on 31 March local time, so it is March usage and is billed on the March invoice.
Anything that reports a month of usage uses the same rule: the monthly total on the Console usage page, the invoice, and the figure Support gives a customer for a month. Usage before March 2027 stays on UTC periods and is not re-cut."}, {"source": "sources/jira/customer-support/SUP-81234-credit-memo-post-rollout-invoice-adjustment-query.json", "chunk": "2/7", "kind": "Jira ticket", "title": "SUP-81234: Unexpected post-rollout credit memo applied to prior invoice causing balance confusion", "status": "In Progress", "date": "2026-03-12", "text": "description: Issue summary: Customer BrightHealth AI contacted Support after noticing an unexpected credit memo posted on 2026-03-09 that retroactively adjusted a Feb invoice (INV-2026-02-15-001). They were previously charged and reported the Feb invoice as reconciled in their ERP; the new credit appears to reduce that historical invoice and created a negative balance on their account statement.
Impact: Customer finance team is unable to reconcile month-end numbers; they are pausing upcoming committed capacity increases until ledger is clarified. Customer requests explanation, audit trail, and confirmation that no double-refund/duplicate adjustment will be applied.
Environment: Redwood hosted billing system; customer is on Dedicated plan tied to org ID org-brighthealth-01; metering shows normal usage patterns around the Feb rollout of open-llama-13b-v2.
Initial customer-provided artifacts: invoice PDF INV-2026-02-15-001, credit memo CM-2026-03-09-77, billing export CSV (billing_export_2026-03-10.csv), and screenshot of account statement.

### Source of truth
- Redwood internal metering is the operational source of truth for usage delivered.

- Reconciliation is required at least monthly, and weekly during launch/transition periods.
### Minimum reconciliation outputs (monthly close)
For each marketplace (AWS, GCP) and each SKU/dimension:
- Units billed (marketplace) vs units metered (Redwood)
- Gross billed amount (marketplace) vs gross revenue recognized (Redwood)
- Marketplace fees (per statement) vs accrued fees
- Net remittance vs cash received
- Open receivable balance vs “due from marketplace” aging based on remittance schedule"}]}
